source.quote: The requirements of this subdivision do not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to subdivision (2), (3), or (4) of Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Subject to paragraphs (5) and (6), if an initial inspection is conducted pursuant to this subdivision and, at the time of inspection, the premises do not contain tenant possessions that prevent the landlord from identifying repairs or cleanings due to the presence of those possessions, the landlord shall not use the security for deductions for repairs or cleanings that are not identified in the itemized statement described in paragraph (2).

contested.question: When the landlord skipped the written offer of an initial inspection, or did not hold an inspection the tenant requested, may it still deduct repairs and cleanings an inspection would have identified?

branches.reading: Yes. Paragraph (4) bars unlisted deductions only if an initial inspection is conducted. Skipping the notice or the inspection is a violation of the section with no stated bar; its consequence runs through bad-faith damages under subdivision (m). Courts do not add penalties a statute does not provide.

authority.quote: if an initial inspection is conducted pursuant to this subdivision

authority.citation: Granberry v. Islay Investments (1995) 9 Cal.4th 738, 747 [mirror text]
authority.quote: Courts will not impose penalties for noncompliance with statutory provisions in addition to those that are provided expressly or by necessary implication.

effect.statement: Deductions remain available; the skipped duty is exposure under subdivision (m) only if in bad faith.

branches.reading: No. The inspection exists so the tenant can cure and avoid deductions; a landlord who denied that opportunity cannot take deductions an inspection would have identified, and retaining them is a retention in violation of the section.

authority.quote: The purpose of the initial inspection shall be to allow the tenant an opportunity to remedy identified deficiencies, in a manner consistent with the rights and obligations of the parties under the rental agreement, in order to avoid deductions from the security.
The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section
